subject: [PATCH v8 28/30] mm: handle PMD swap entry faults on swap-in

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where PMD (Page Map Directory) swap entries would fault indefinitely when trying to swap in a huge page. The patch introduces a new function, do_huge_pmd_swap_page(), which resolves the whole mapping at PMD granularity and handles various failure cases, such as cache splitting or allocation failures. It also ensures that the folio is properly dropped from the swap cache if it has never been mapped or is not up-to-date. The patch aims to prevent a transient PMD-order allocation failure from becoming a VM_FAULT_OOM error.

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lance Yang expressed concern that the patch does not handle the case where a PMD swap entry is split due to cache insertion losing a race, and suggested that this edge case should be addressed.

The reviewer pointed out a potential race condition in the swap cache handling, where zswap writeback may insert an order-0 folio into the cache while another thread is still accessing it. This can lead to the last reference to the folio being dropped prematurely, causing issues with I/O completion. The reviewer suggested unlocking and putting the folio on size mismatch, then jumping to split_fallback to keep the folio in the swap cache for do_swap_page().

Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a PMD swap entry is split due to cache insertion losing a race, and requested additional locking to prevent this issue.

2026-10-04.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where PMD (Page Map Directory) swap entries would fault indefinitely when swapped out, causing a VM_FAULT_OOM error. The solution is to split the PMD entry into individual PTEs and return 0, allowing the retry to land in do_swap_page(). This approach ensures that transient allocation failures do not become permanent errors. Additionally, the patch handles various edge cases, such as dropping folios from the swap cache when necessary, refusing to map poisoned subpages, and calling wp_huge_pmd() for write faults on read-only PMDs.
